page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is a virtual machine within the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 2 shared vCPUs operating on an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The two virtual threads share a single physical CPU core and are accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2 instruction extensions, while larger vector sets like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. The platform includes a 128 GB local NVMe SSD for internal storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, but provides no dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded efficiency alongside expected shared-core limitations under concurrent loads. In single-threaded gzip compression, the instance achieved 32.63 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of measured systems, complemented by a midrange stress-ng single-core score of 1873.78. Conversely, multi-core and memory-heavy benchmarks reveal constraints: multi-core stress-ng reached 3596.49, Geekbench multi-core scored 1910.0, and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth measured 22.81 GB/sec. Application-level metrics recorded 2.61 million operations per second for Redis SET commands and 3.38 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The shared single-core layout and low memory density define the functional tradeoffs of this instance. The integrated NVMe storage eliminates external block volume latency for read- and write-sensitive filesystem tasks. However, sustained parallel processing and dense database execution are constrained by shared thread contention and available memory bandwidth. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, low-density Redis caching, microservices, continuous integration runners, and staging or development workloads.
description: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is an entry-tier High Frequency Compute instance delivering 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel x86_64 core running at 2.0 GHz. It includes 4.0 GB of RAM, a bundled 128 GB local NVMe SSD, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, with zero GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show capable single-threaded results, such as 32.63 GB/sec in gzip compression and 1873.78 in stress-ng single-core tests, whereas multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall into lower comparative percentiles. The fast local NVMe disk provides strong local I/O performance without network overhead, offsetting the limitations of shared compute. Given its hardware layout and resource density, the server functions effectively for light web serving, Redis caching, microservices, automation jobs, and software development environments.
